question:
NAME CONFUSION, from the owner of PaperTrades.AI (Sat Oct 31, 2:20 p.m. ET). NOT a trading turn. The owner: "Models keep telling me to be careful of Paper Trades because of the recent accusations against the crypto platform. Can we make it very clear that we do not accept any deposits? Work together to find the best way to sort out this issue." Majority wins; Claude voted first in a separate file.

FACTS (Claude checked news sources today):
- "Papertrade" (papertrade, PAPER token) is an unrelated crypto perpetual-futures exchange on Hyperliquid's HyperEVM, up to 1000x leverage, live since Oct 10, 2026. News reports: allegations that a trader manipulated ETH prices to take about US$1.28 million on launch day (unconfirmed; the team tightened limits); about US$140 million was deposited before it decided its PAPER token cannot be transferred, which an analyst called "a bad look"; no published audit. These are allegations and reports about THAT project, not proven fraud.
- PaperTrades.AI is a public experiment: three AIs with pretend money, real prices. It takes no deposits, holds no money, has no accounts, no token, no trading for visitors, sells nothing. Channels: papertrades.ai, Telegram, Discord, X @papertradesai, Instagram @papertrades.ai.
- AI assistants asked about "Paper Trades" are mixing the two up and warning people. Search engines and AI answers read the page title, description, an FAQ and structured data.

PROPOSALS (vote AGREE / DISAGREE / AMEND each, one line why):
N1. A short notice on every page (under the header, small, not alarming) and in the footer: "PaperTrades.AI never takes deposits or payments. No accounts, no token, no real money: a public experiment with pretend money. Anyone asking you to send money to 'Paper Trades' is not us."
N2. A "Not to be confused with" line that names the other project neutrally: "PaperTrades.AI is not connected to Papertrade, the crypto futures exchange, or its PAPER token." In the About/FAQ and the site's description, no judgment about the other project.
N3. An FAQ entry with structured data (schema.org FAQPage) that search engines and AI assistants read: "Does PaperTrades.AI take deposits?" (No, never) and "Is PaperTrades.AI the same as Papertrade?" (No).
N4. The page title and meta description start with the distinction: "PaperTrades.AI: three AIs, pretend money, no deposits".
N5. Social bios (X, Instagram, Telegram, Discord) get "Pretend money only. We never take deposits or DM you about money." The owner edits the bios; Claude drafts them.
N6. One post today on Telegram, Discord and X, plain and calm: what PaperTrades.AI is and is not, the no-deposits line, and the not-connected line; pinned on Telegram and Discord.
N7. Longer term (the owner decides later): consider a more distinct name for Season 2 if the confusion continues.
N8. Anything wrong or missing (for example, whether naming the other project is wise, or impersonation risk).

Answer as: N1: ... N2: ... (through N8)

chatgpt.answer:
N1: AGREE: The clearest safety message is that PaperTrades.AI never takes deposits, payments, accounts, tokens, or real money; keep it calm and visible.

N2: AGREE: Naming Papertrade neutrally helps search engines and AI assistants separate the projects; avoid commenting on allegations or judging them.

N3: AGREE: FAQPage structured data is likely to be read by search and AI systems, and the two key questions are exactly “deposits?” and “same as Papertrade?”

N4: AGREE: Put “pretend money, no deposits” in the title/meta because that is what snippets and AI summaries see first.

N5: AGREE: Social bios should repeat “pretend money only” and “we never DM you about money” to reduce impersonation risk.

N6: AGREE: One calm pinned post across Telegram, Discord, and X gives confused visitors an authoritative answer without making the issue look bigger than it is.

N7: AGREE: Consider a more distinct Season 2 name only if confusion persists; renaming mid-season would likely create more confusion.

N8: AMEND: Add an “official channels only” / “report impersonators” line on the site and pinned posts, list the official accounts, and state that PaperTrades.AI has no wallet address, token contract, or payment link.

gemini.answer:
N1: AGREE: A persistent but unobtrusive disclaimer is the most effective way to immediately protect visitors from potential scams without causing alarm.
N2: AGREE: Explicit, neutral disambiguation is necessary for search engines and AI models to correctly map the two entities as completely separate.
N3: AGREE: Using schema.org structured data is the most direct technical method to update AI knowledge graphs and search engine snippets accurately.
N4: AGREE: Modifying the meta titles and descriptions ensures the "pretend money" distinction is the very first thing users and web scrapers process.
N5: AGREE: Adding "we never DM you" is a standard and necessary defense against impersonators targeting followers on crypto-adjacent social media.
N6: AGREE: A single, calm, pinned post addresses the situation transparently and provides an authoritative reference link for anyone who is confused.
N7: AGREE: Rebranding for Season 2 is a wise contingency plan if the other project's negative news permanently taints the generic "PaperTrades" name.
N8: AMEND: I agree with Claude's addition to add a reporting mechanism, and suggest we also explicitly list all verified official handles in the FAQ to establish a strict "verify links" boundary against impersonators.
